glance.question: How should evangelicals describe the relations of Father, Son and Spirit?

positions.name: Classical Trinitarianism
positions.claim: One God in three equal persons; the Son's submission belongs to his incarnation, not eternity.

positions.name: Eternal Submission of the Son
positions.claim: The Son is equal in being but eternally submits to the Father's authority.

positions.name: Social Trinitarianism
positions.claim: The three persons form an eternal communion that models human community.

start_here.title: 10 Things You Should Know about the Trinity
start_here.author: Fred Sanders
start_here.why: Ten short points on what the doctrine says and why it belongs to the gospel.

start_here.title: How EFS Muddles Christology and the Gospel
start_here.author: Samuel G. Parkison
start_here.why: A classical theologian's case that eternal functional subordination confuses the Son's two natures.

start_here.title: Does Complementarianism Depend on ERAS?
start_here.author: Stephen J. Wellum
start_here.why: A complementarian who rejects eternal authority relations explains why the two questions can be separated.

key_number.text: In 2025, 97% of Americans with evangelical beliefs agreed there is one true God in three persons, but only 41% disagreed that the Holy Spirit is a force and not a personal being.

notes: Position 2's card title was 'Evangelical Tritheism / Soft Subordinationism', labels its holders reject; renamed 2026-11-14 (team4 V3) to 'Eternal Submission of the Son (ERAS, also called EFS)'. Ware uses ERAS in his own words: secundumscripturas.com, July 4 2016. Grudem verified in his own words: ETS Nov 15 2016 handout, 'The names Father and Son indicate an eternal relationship of authority and submission.' https://www.waynegrudem.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/ETS-Presentation-on-Trinity-11-15-16.pdf. His voice page is noindex, so the name prints as plain text. Other card names not verified this session; none added. 97% is Lifeway's printed figure (white paper p.7 and report p.43).
